modules.name: Georeference, true-north and solar frame
modules.design_question: Where is the site, which way is true north in the normalised model, and where is the sun, as explicit UTC instants and Vancouver clock time, at every study instant other modules need?
modules.effort: M: about 6-7 dev-days (r1 estimate 3-4; r2 adds SitePlacement, up-axis normalisation, per-rule clock basis and a blocking direction check; r3 adds explicit UTC instants, a runtime clock self-test, a 1-min sun table and label-aligned mirror check, about 1 more)
inputs: Layer 0 model with import metadata: up axis (Y-up or Z-up), handedness, units (r2)

SitePlacement: georeferenced block polygon (WGS84), how it was placed and project CRS; first-ranked source is the VTC site-plan package (request it now with a team member's own email, r3); else a team choice among 3-5 candidate blocks narrowed by the brief's cues (station on the neighbouring site, transit plaza diagonally across, arterial on a long side, retail high street); default centre about 49.283 N, 123.12 W; user-editable
North reference, highest confidence first: site-plan north arrow, IFC TrueNorth (2D direction in the project XY plane, default [0,1]), Rhino North setting, Revit True North

Study calendar: dates, local clock times and per-rule time-zone fields: literal clause zone text, literal clause UTC offset, tzdata offset (tzdata 2026b or later); each rule instant is converted once, server-side, to an explicit UTC timestamp (r3)

Site-plan direction labels (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet and North Shore Mountains) placed in the model frame: a georegistered VTC site-plan underlay in the same import, or the user's picks of the block edge facing each label (r3)

parameters.name: North angle (model +Y to true north)
parameters.relationship: Every shadow, sun-hour and facade result rotates with this angle; 45 degrees of error swaps one downtown street axis for the other. Ladybug north_angle = Rhino North - 90; IFC TrueNorth (x, y) gives atan2(-x, y) (derived).

parameters.name: Street-grid rotation vs true north
parameters.relationship: Downtown grid is rotated about 45 degrees (Granville about 045, West Georgia about 315, from OSM geometry), so street-aligned facades face NE/SE/SW/NW; orientation classes must use true north, not model axes.

parameters.name: Up axis and handedness of the import
parameters.relationship: Y-up files (glTF, three.js) need a +90 degree turn about X to reach Z-up; a plain Y/Z swap has determinant -1 and mirrors the plan, so a NW shadow lands NE or SW (derived). OBJ defines no up axis.

parameters.name: Clock basis per rule
parameters.relationship: Rules name their own zone: 22 Sept PDT (UTC-7), cenotaph PST (UTC-8). BC runs on UTC-7 all year since 8 Mar 2026, so 10:00 PST on 11 Nov reads 11:00 on the wall clock. Store each instant as explicit UTC.

parameters.name: Latitude and solar noon
parameters.relationship: At 49.28 N the noon sun is 40.8 degrees high at the equinox and 17.3 at the winter solstice (shadow 1.16 and 3.21 times height). Solar noon: 13:05 UTC-7 on 22 Sept, 11:56 UTC-8 on 11 Nov (NOAA-algorithm recomputation, r3 own code).

parameters.name: Solar-position algorithm
parameters.relationship: Shadow-edge error equals error angle times shadow length; SunCalc 2.x states about 0.08 degrees (under 1 m on a 600 m shadow, derived), degrees clockwise from north, refraction-corrected altitude. Pin 2.1.1. pvlib spa_python gives NREL SPA with apparent_elevation.

parameters.name: Grid convergence of a UTM model
parameters.relationship: In UTM zone 10 (City DEM CRS) grid north differs from true north by about 0.09 degrees at 123.12 W (convergence = delta lambda x sin phi, derived), negligible beside the 1-degree tolerance but recorded.

parameters.name: Sun-table resolution for swept windows
parameters.relationship: On 22 Sept azimuth moves 3.6-5.0 degrees per 15 min; a 305 m shadow tip moves up to 174 m per 15 min on 11 Nov (wall clock). M02 therefore hulls consecutive instants from a 1-min SunTable (derived, r3).

parameters.name: Label placement for the mirror check
parameters.relationship: The check needs the label directions in the model frame. Without an underlay or edge picks it compares the rotated model with itself and cannot see a reflection (r3 critique).

metrics.name: Model-north agreement between explicit references
metrics.good: Explicit references (site-plan arrow, IFC TrueNorth, Rhino North, Revit True North) agree within 1 degree; OSM-implied grid bearing within about 3 degrees
metrics.bad: Explicit references disagree by more than 1 degree, or none exists: block downstream modules and ask the user. OSM disagreement above about 3 degrees: warning only
metrics.basis: Editable tolerances for drawing precision. OSM bearing is only an estimate for a hypothetical site, so it warns but never blocks (r1 change). The 1-degree tolerance feeds the INDETERMINATE band in P02-M02 (r2).
metrics.method: Compare north arrow, IFC TrueNorth / Rhino North, and OSM street-bearing-implied angle.

metrics.name: Assuming model +Y is true north
metrics.good: North angle read from the site-plan arrow; expect roughly 45 degrees offset for a street-aligned model
metrics.bad: Treating drawing-up as north on this site
metrics.basis: City states the downtown grid is rotated (re-read r3); OSM bearings of Granville (about 44.7 deg) and West Georgia (about 314.8 deg) computed for this packet and reproduced by the round-1 reviewer. The VTC brief also says the north arrow is rotated.

metrics.name: Time-zone offset per study date and rule
metrics.good: 22 Sept 2026 = UTC-7; 11 Nov 2026 = UTC-7 under BC's year-round Pacific Time (tzdata 2026b or later); each rule stores its literal clause zone and offset and an explicit UTC instant (22 Sept 10:00 = 17:00Z; 11 Nov reading A 10:00 UTC-8 = 18:00Z; reading B 10:00 UTC-7 = 17:00Z), with a mismatch banner (cenotaph: PST = UTC-8)
metrics.bad: One fixed offset for all rules; tzdata older than 2026b (gives UTC-8 on 11 Nov); trusting the clause label or tz abbreviation; or converting local time to UTC in the browser, whose ICU/CLDR data may predate 2026b
metrics.basis: v1 said all policy hours are PDT; r1 said 11 Nov is PST because DST ended 1 Nov 2026; r2: BC moved to UTC-7 permanently on 8 Mar 2026 (BC Gov release, opened) and tz 2026b models UTC-7 from 1 Nov 2026 with abbreviation MST. r3: a build-time tzdata pin does not govern the entrant's browser (tz NEWS: the 1 Nov 2026 date is a CLDR 48.1 workaround; older slim zic files may ignore it), so instants are stored as UTC. Clause wording on the cenotaph rule is still reviewer relay.
metrics.method: Server: unit-test tzdata 2026b or later (22 Sept and 11 Nov give -7); fail the build if older. Client: no local-time Date constructors or Intl time zones in any compute path (lint rule) plus the runtime self-test below. Never branch on the tz abbreviation.

metrics.name: Runtime clock self-test (explicit UTC instants)
metrics.good: At start-up and before every M02 run assert: 22 Sept 2026 10:00 = 2026-09-22T17:00:00Z; 11 Nov reading A 10:00 = 2026-11-11T18:00:00Z; reading B 10:00 = 2026-11-11T17:00:00Z; sun at 17:00Z on 11 Nov = 12.65 deg altitude and 137.2 deg azimuth (tolerance 0.2)
metrics.bad: Any mismatch: block M02 and any module using rule instants, and print which environment (browser, ICU, tzdata version) produced it
metrics.basis: r3 critique: reading B collapses into reading A (UTC-8) in a browser whose tz data predates 2026b, which silently drops the 09:00-11:00 PST window with the longest reach (about 1,340 m) and returns a false PASS. Expected values are arithmetic on the BC release (opened) and tz NEWS (opened); sun values recomputed with the NOAA equations (r3 own code).
metrics.method: Run the same assertions in the browser and on the server; record userAgent and tz-data version in the result header; the UTC instant needs no tz database once stored.

metrics.name: Sun-position error
metrics.good: At most 0.1 degree (SunCalc 2.x README states about 0.08)
metrics.bad: Above 0.5 degree (unvalidated implementation)
metrics.basis: Good value from the SunCalc README (opened; Meeus algorithms validated against JPL Horizons and USNO); bad value is an editable preset. Regression tolerance 0.2 degree because apparent (refraction) and geometric altitudes differ by 0.15 degree near 6 degrees.
metrics.method: Unit-test pinned suncalc 2.1.1 against pvlib spa_python (apparent elevation) for Vancouver at 17:00Z, 20:05Z, 23:00Z on 22 Sept (fixtures: 26.9 deg / 125.9 deg at 10:00 UTC-7; 28.2 / 231.6 at 16:00), 17:00Z and 18:00Z on 11 Nov (12.65 / 137.2; 18.4 / 150.7) and 09:00 UTC-8 on 21 Dec (about 6 degrees, refraction matters).

metrics.name: Named-direction (mirror) check
metrics.good: Labels placed in the model frame; after normalisation and rotation Stanley Park lies NW, BC Place SE and Burrard Inlet N-NE of the SitePlacement centroid, each within a +/-30 degree sector; the L-fixture passes all four axis reflections (N-S, E-W, NW-SE, NE-SW), where only the Burrard Inlet sector catches NW-SE (derived)
metrics.bad: Any direction outside its sector: block M02 and warn elsewhere until the axes are fixed or the user overrides with a logged reason. No labels in the model frame: state NOT CHECKABLE and block M02 PASS/FAIL badges
metrics.basis: Directions are labelled on the VTC site plan; the sectors are rough geography from the r2 critique and the tolerance is an editable preset. A mirror error passes every angle check, so the test is blocking (r2). r3: the check only works if the labels are in the model frame; unit test: Y/Z-swapped import of the L-fixture plus underlay fails.
metrics.method: Compute bearings from OSM or City-data centroids at build time; compare with the label bearings in the model frame after rotation; add an asymmetric L-shaped fixture and fail on any reflection (determinant -1), testing all four axis mirrors.

modules.method: 1) Normalise every import to right-handed, Z-up, metres: record up axis and handedness; Y-up becomes Z-up by +90 degrees about X, never a Y/Z swap (determinant +1). 2) Georeference with SitePlacement (VTC package first; UTM zone 10, NAD83 CSRS). 3) Take north from the highest-confidence source; store as angle CCW from +Y (Ladybug north_angle = Rhino North - 90). 4) Convert each rule's local time, literal clause offset and tzdata offset once, server-side, into explicit UTC instants; never convert local time in the browser. 5) Compute apparent altitude and azimuth from UTC (suncalc 2.1.1 or pvlib spa_python) at 15-min instants and a 1-min SunTable; rotate into the model frame. 6) Run the runtime self-test and the named-direction check; block M02 on failure, and block all modules if explicit north references disagree by more than 1 degree. 7) Emit NorthFrame, SitePlacement, SunVectorSet, SweepWindow.
visualization: Stereographic sun-path diagram with equinox and solstice arcs; the 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 UTC-7 window and both readings of the 11 Nov window (UTC-8 literal, UTC-7 wall clock) in three colours; far-horizon profile shaded when loaded
Plan view with three arrows (model Y, true north, street-grid bearing); red banner when explicit references disagree, amber when only OSM disagrees
Rotated site plan with the brief's named directions drawn as +/-30 degree sector wedges and a pass / fail / NOT CHECKABLE tick per sector (mirror check), label anchors drawn on the underlay
Rule clock table: clause zone text, clause offset, tzdata offset and explicit UTC instant per rule, mismatch badge, and a green or red runtime self-test lamp with the environment string
outputs: NorthFrame {angle_ccw_from_Y_deg, source, confidence, up_axis_in, handedness_in, transform_det}
SitePlacement {polygon_wgs84, crs, source, rationale, candidate_blocks[], brief_cues_used}
SunVectorSet [{rule_id, local_time, utc_instant, clause_zone_text, clause_utc_offset_h, tzdata_offset_h, tzdata_version, azimuth_true_deg, apparent_altitude_deg, vector_model_frame}]
SweepWindow {rule_id, utc_start, utc_end, instants_15min[], sun_table_1min[]}

StudyCalendar presets: BasicStudy 22 Sept 10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00 UTC-7 (17, 19, 21, 23Z; submission format only); DetailedStudy 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 every 15 min (25 instants); RemembranceDay reading A 10:00-12:00 UTC-8 (18:00-20:00Z) and reading B 10:00-12:00 UTC-7 (17:00-19:00Z), 15-min step, 9 instants each (step is a team assumption); optional 20 Mar, 21 Jun, 21 Dec (design exploration; further dates may be required by s.3.1.4)
modules.human_judgment: Confirm which north the site plan uses and its sign; confirm where the hypothetical block sits and why; choose study dates beyond the policy dates; decide which clock reading of the 11 Nov rule to follow (ask the City at cddg@vancouver.ca, not the competition organisers); prefer a surveyed grid angle over the OSM estimate.
modules.limits: North stays an input unless the file stores it. The OSM grid bearing (about 45 degrees) is an estimate, not a survey. Magnetic declination is not applied. Solar algorithms ignore terrain and atmosphere; far horizons are added in other modules. Named-direction sectors are rough geography and need label placement. Results depend on the clock basis the user selects.

libraries.name: SunCalc (JS), pinned at 2.1.1 with a lockfile integrity hash
libraries.role: in-browser sun position from UTC epoch (degrees clockwise from north, refraction-corrected altitude)

libraries.name: IANA tz database, release 2026b or later (server side only)
libraries.role: UTC offsets per date at data-build time; models BC's permanent UTC-7

libraries.name: pyproj
libraries.role: CRS transforms (UTM zone 10 NAD83 CSRS to WGS84), grid convergence

modules.name: Vancouver downtown solar-access test and solar envelope
modules.design_question: Does the proposal add shadow to protected public spaces under the Downtown Peninsula guidelines over each rule's continuous window, and what maximum height does each footprint cell allow?
modules.effort: XL: about 21-26 dev-days in two stages, plus 3-5 data dev-days (PDF transcription with second reader, Table-1 polygons, approved towers, VTC model). Stage A for 13 Nov (about 15-18): Table-1 v0 in EXPLORATION mode, terrain, three scenarios, swept-window test, robust PASS/FAIL/INDETERMINATE behind the evidence gate, continuous envelope, UTC rule table. Stage B by 10 Dec (about 6-8): Detailed tables, 11 Nov dual readings, coverage %, exception stub, block sensitivity, tower-position sweep, board sheet.
inputs: SweepWindow, 1-min SunTable, SunVectorSet (explicit UTC instants), NorthFrame and SitePlacement from P02-M01
Proposed massing (Layer 0 geometry), split into convex parts per tier for the swept-shadow hull

Context scenarios: existing plus approved built context; plus known proposed developments (user import). Source order: VTC package 3D model if it carries context (request now); else City 'Building footprints 2009' extruded by hgt_agl, with post-2009 and approved towers added by hand, each with a source
Terrain mesh from City DEM (1 m cells, 2013 LiDAR, UTM zone 10 NAD83 CSRS), LiDAR 2022 or contours (Open Government Licence - Vancouver) covering the site and every protected space

Versioned Table-1 protected-space GeoJSON: polygon, class, clause, hours, literal zone, total-or-new-shadow basis, time basis (discrete, continuous or unknown), per-rule evidence level, exception flags; rule-set metadata: source title, approval date, last amended, effective date, superseded-check date, PDF SHA-256, page refs, transcriber, second reader, primary_opened flag
Hand-checked crosswalk from Table-1 classes to Park Board classes (Park Board class is never used to derive a Table-1 class)

Study preset (BasicStudy, DetailedStudy, RemembranceDay readings A and B, hourly exploration); robustness settings (north tolerance, geometric tolerance, noise-floor cell size); 3-5 candidate blocks chosen from the brief's cues; tower-position grid and rotation step for the sweep

parameters.name: Protected-space class (Table 1)
parameters.relationship: Class selects clause and result type: parks, schools and s.4.2 plazas get a 0 m2 test (3.1.1); other plazas and West End miniparks only minimise (3.2.1); Villages use the north sidewalk (3.3.1). Misclassifying a space flips pass/fail.

parameters.name: Study window and clock basis per rule
parameters.relationship: Parks and schools 10:00-16:00 on 22 Sept (UTC-7; 17:00-23:00Z); Davie 10:00-16:00, Robson 10:00-15:00; cenotaph 10:00-12:00 PST on 11 Nov: literal 18:00-20:00Z, wall-clock reading 17:00-19:00Z reaches farther.

parameters.name: Compliance time basis (instants or continuous)
parameters.relationship: Between 15-min instants a 300 m shadow tip moves up to 59 m (22 Sept) and 305 m up to 174 m (11 Nov, wall clock); 2-hour instants leave 33-39 degree azimuth gaps. A swept window cannot miss a small space; instants can.

parameters.name: Tower height H
parameters.relationship: Shadow length is H / tan(altitude). 300 m throws about 590 m (10:00) and 560 m (16:00) on 22 Sept; on 11 Nov about 905 m at 10:00 PST (18.4 degrees) and 1,340 m at 09:00 PST (12.7 degrees).

parameters.name: Shadow bearing
parameters.relationship: On 22 Sept the shadow bearing sweeps 306 (10:00), 339, 18 to 52 degrees (16:00); on 11 Nov 331-1 (10:00-12:00 PST) or 317-346 (09:00-11:00 PST). Spaces NW to NE of the tower are at risk.

parameters.name: Level difference to the protected space
parameters.relationship: A receiver lying dz below the site adds about dz x 1.9-2.0 m of shadow reach at 10:00 and 16:00 on 22 Sept; 20 m of fall moves a shadow edge about 40 m, enough to flip pass/fail (derived).

parameters.name: Floor-plate width perpendicular to the sun
parameters.relationship: Wider plate gives a wider shadow band and longer dwell time on any point (geometry). The City ties larger tower floor plates to solar-access compliance (2024 report, not opened).

parameters.name: Tower position and rotation on the block
parameters.relationship: Moving the tower 10 m toward a space moves each shadow edge 10 m toward it; rotating the plate changes the width across the sun. The sweep maps both over the 79.2 x 144.8 m block (geometry).

parameters.name: Exception requested
parameters.relationship: A fail becomes a case-by-case exception only for social housing, below-market rental, public childcare, heritage conservation or a major city-building priority (3.1.2), with a rationale statement and Detailed study (5.2). Council removed the blanket social-housing exemption.

parameters.name: Instant spacing and count N
parameters.relationship: Basic uses 4 instants, Detailed 25 at 15 min, the 11 Nov window 9 per reading. The swept hull needs consecutive instants at most 15 min apart (chord deviation 0.4 m at 305 m on 11 Nov). Coverage % takes N, not 25.

parameters.name: Baseline scenario choice
parameters.relationship: New shadow is measured against existing plus approved context with topography; adding known proposed developments to the baseline lowers the new shadow attributed to the proposal where shadows overlap, so the scenario must be stated (5.1).

parameters.name: Baseline context extent
parameters.relationship: Extent = site reach disc plus each in-reach space's sun wedge, radius (H_max + level difference) / tan(lowest altitude in its window). The disc suffices for new shadow along a ray (derived); existing, cumulative and total-shadow figures need the wedges.

parameters.name: Site placement (which block)
parameters.relationship: The block's position decides which Table-1 spaces fall within shadow reach (about 0.6 km on 22 Sept, up to 1.4 km for 305 m on 11 Nov); the same massing can pass on one block and fail on another.

parameters.name: North and geometry tolerance
parameters.relationship: A north error of 1 degree moves a shadow tip L x tan(1 deg): about 10 m at 590 m, 16 m at 905 m, 24 m at 1.4 km (derived), enough to flip a 0 m2 result.

parameters.name: Numerical noise floor
parameters.relationship: Floor = one raster cell area, capped at 0.5% of the space area (team presets); slivers under 0.1 m wide are listed separately. A 'no shadow' rule gets floor 0: sliver-only exceedance reads INDETERMINATE, never PASS.

parameters.name: Rule-set version and effective date
parameters.relationship: The CDDG takes effect 27 Oct 2026 and may replace the July 2026 text before entrants submit; results are valid only for the stamped rule-set version, and a version change invalidates cached PolicyResults.

parameters.name: Total or new shadow, per rule
parameters.relationship: Parks test new shadow (proposal minus baseline); the cenotaph rule reads 'no shadow'. If it means total shadow, an existing tower's shadow fails it and no baseline offsets it; default to total, show both, transcribe the basis per rule.

metrics.name: New shadow on parks and schools (community, neighbourhood, local parks; school sites), inside property lines
metrics.good: 0 m2 over the whole window 10:00-16:00 on 22 Sept (3.1.1); ROBUST PASS only if it also holds under the perturbation set
metrics.bad: Above the noise floor anywhere in the window: FAIL (INDETERMINATE inside the perturbation band); exception case (3.1.2) or cut the massing
metrics.basis: UDI (opened): 22 Sept 10 am-4 pm PDT for school sites and community, neighbourhood and local parks; Daily Hive (opened): most new shadow prohibited 10-16 on 22 Sept. Clause numbers and area tolerance rest on the round-1 reviewer's reading of the PDF (approved 17 Sept 2025, amended 29 July 2026), which no team member has opened. r3: split from the plaza rule so each carries its own evidence level.
metrics.method: Swept-shadow hull of the proposal minus the baseline, clipped to each property-line polygon; slivers below the floor listed separately; badge shown only in COMPLIANCE mode.

metrics.name: Plazas moved up to the park rule: Jack Poole Plaza, Robson Square, Dilawri Square South
metrics.good: 0 m2 over the whole window 10:00-16:00 on 22 Sept (3.1 via 4.2.1); exceptions possible under 3.1.2
metrics.bad: Any new shadow with no exception case
metrics.basis: Replaces v1 'Library Square south plaza: absolute no new shadow', taken from draft coverage (S06). Daily Hive (S04, opened) names Robson Square and Jack Poole Plaza as specially protected, without timing; the routing to the s.3.1 park rule, exception availability and Dilawri Square South rest on the reviewer alone.

metrics.name: Other urban plazas and West End miniparks (not upgraded by s.4.2)
metrics.unit: m2 and coverage % over the window
metrics.good: No pass/fail: report new-shadow m2 and coverage % and show that reductions were tried 'where possible' (3.2.1)
metrics.bad: A 0 m2 pass/fail applied to them, or no report
metrics.basis: v1 applied the zero-shadow test to all plazas and miniparks; the reviewer's reading of 3.2.1 says only minimise where possible. Reviewer relay only; the City page titles Decision Tree B for West End minipark and urban plaza (S01, re-read r3) but the tree itself was not opened.

metrics.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Garden/Park
metrics.good: No new shadow over the window 10:00-16:00 on 22 Sept (4.1.1); reportedly the only rule with no exception clause
metrics.bad: Any new shadow
metrics.basis: r3: downgraded from verified_secondary. The absolute rule and 'no exception clause' rest on the 2025 draft coverage (S06, superseded text) and the reviewer's reading; Daily Hive (S04) names the garden among specially protected spaces without timing, which does not corroborate either point.

metrics.name: Davie Village north sidewalk, 10:00-16:00
metrics.unit: m2 over the window (curb to building face)
metrics.good: 0 m2 over the window 10:00-16:00 on 22 Sept (3.3.1(a))
metrics.bad: Above the noise floor anywhere in the window
metrics.basis: r3: split from the Village metric. UDI (S07, opened) names the north sidewalk of Davie Village under the 22 Sept 10 am-4 pm PDT study; the draft (S06) agrees on 10-16. Clause number 3.3.1 and the curb-to-face extent are reviewer relay; Map 2 not opened.

metrics.name: Robson Village north sidewalk, 10:00-15:00
metrics.unit: m2 over the window (curb to building face)
metrics.good: 0 m2 over the window 10:00-15:00 on 22 Sept (3.3.1(b))
metrics.bad: Above the noise floor anywhere in the window
metrics.basis: r3: split and downgraded. Only the 2025 draft (S06) gives 10-15; UDI (final) says Robson is 'similar' without hours; clause 3.3.1(b) and Map 3 are reviewer relay.

metrics.name: Victory Square cenotaph circle
metrics.good: No shadow on the circle during the 11 Nov window (4.3.1), run under both clock readings: A 10:00-12:00 UTC-8 (18:00-20:00Z), B 10:00-12:00 UTC-7 (17:00-19:00Z); basis defaults to total shadow, new shadow also shown; PASS only if both pass; noise floor 0 (sliver-only exceedance is INDETERMINATE); exceptions only after comprehensive engagement (4.3.2)
metrics.bad: Any shadow on the circle in either window
metrics.basis: v1 said 11:00 on Remembrance Day (draft coverage, S05, S06). Approved text per reviewer: 10:00-12:00 PST. r2: BC has run on UTC-7 all year since 8 Mar 2026 (S55), so literal PST and the wall clock differ by one hour; Daily Hive says only 'Remembrance Day mornings'. r3: total shadow is the default (conservative); the questions go to the City, not the competition organisers. Victory Square is outside the CDDG area (S09) but inside this guideline.

metrics.name: Assessment dates and window
metrics.good: 22 Sept only (plus 11 Nov for the cenotaph), per-rule windows; spring equinox optional extra; further dates may be required (3.1.4)
metrics.bad: Spring-equinox (20/21 Mar) test treated as required downtown, or 22 Sept run on the wrong clock
metrics.basis: Downtown guidelines eliminated the spring-equinox consideration (Daily Hive and UDI, both opened; UDI dates the 4 Feb 2026 amendment, matching the 4 Feb 2026 committee agenda S61). Clause 3.1.4 is reviewer relay.

metrics.name: Basic Shadow Study sheet (submission format, not compliance)
metrics.good: 4 instants (10, 12, 14, 16 UTC-7; 17, 19, 21, 23Z), geolocated, complete context with terrain, new shadow visually delineated from existing (5.1); sheet labelled 'format, not compliance'
metrics.bad: Missing instants, wrong time zone, flat ground or incomplete context; or the 4 instants used as the compliance or envelope basis
metrics.basis: r3: downgraded from verified_secondary. UDI (opened) names a fall-equinox Basic Shadow Study, which is the only opened support; the 4 instants, UTC-7 and delineation are the reviewer's reading of ss.5.1-5.2 plus v1 search excerpts (2-hour intervals), not stated by any opened source.

metrics.name: Detailed study outputs and Shadow Coverage %
metrics.good: N instants (25 at 15 min for 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 inclusive) with m2 take-offs of existing, proposed-additional and cumulative shadow; coverage % = sum of interval areas / (space area x N) (5.2(b)-(c)); cumulative figures use the receiver-centred context
metrics.bad: An exception sought without a Detailed study
metrics.basis: Formula and 25-instant count quoted only by the round-1 reviewer (relay); no numeric coverage limit was reported, so none is applied. N is a parameter because the 11 Nov window at 15 min has 9 instants (r2).

metrics.name: Window coverage of the compliance test (swept window)
metrics.good: Compliance and envelope computed from a swept window: hull of shadows between consecutive instants at most 15 min apart, per convex part, buffered by the chord deviation (0.4 m worst case), or 1-min sub-sampling; the time basis (instants or continuous) is transcribed per rule and defaults to continuous
metrics.bad: Compliance or envelope from the 4 Basic instants alone, or from instants spaced wider than the smallest receiver
metrics.basis: r3 critique, reproduced: 22 Sept azimuth moves 33.0, 39.0 and 33.7 degrees across the 2-hour steps; a 300 m shadow tip moves 30-59 m per 15 min on 22 Sept and a 305 m tip 57-174 m on 11 Nov (wall clock). Equinox shadow tips run on straight lines (chord deviation 0.002 m); 11 Nov deviates 0.4 m per 15 min and 0.04 m per 5 min (derived). Whether the City judges instants or continuously is not transcribed.
metrics.method: For each convex part and each consecutive instant pair, hull the two shadow polygons; union the hulls; buffer by the chord deviation; run the perturbation set on the hull.

metrics.name: Baseline and context completeness
metrics.good: Complete built and approved context with topography; extent = site reach disc plus receiver sun wedges, radius (H_max + level difference) / tan(lowest altitude in the rule window): about 0.6 km for 22 Sept, about 1.4 km for 305 m if the 11 Nov wall-clock reading applies; known proposed developments as a separate scenario; trees and shade structures excluded (5.1, 5.1.1)
metrics.bad: Flat ground plane, partial context, a fixed 1 km radius, a site-centred disc used for existing, cumulative or total-shadow figures, or trees counted in the baseline. A space whose wedge relies on 2009 footprints prints 'baseline incomplete: new shadow overstated (conservative)'
metrics.basis: v1 projected prisms onto a flat ground plane; r1 set about 1 km; r2 radius follows the lowest altitude per rule window. r3 critique: baseline towers can stand up to the shadow reach beyond a receiver. Derived: along one sun ray a site-centred disc already holds every blocker for new shadow, but existing, cumulative and total shadow depend on all towers within reach of the receiver, so wedges are added. Missing context lowers the baseline shadow and overstates new shadow (conservative for compliance, over-restrictive for the envelope). City 'Building footprints 2009' (S52) is approximate and predates later towers.
metrics.method: List every hand-added approved tower with its source and height; flag each space whose wedge relies on 2009 footprints.

metrics.name: Site plan and context source recorded
metrics.good: VTC 'SITE PLANS & 3D MODEL' package requested and recorded as a source with format, CRS, units, north arrow and context content; it is the first-ranked SitePlacement and context source; candidate blocks justified from the brief's cues
metrics.bad: City 2009 footprints used and a candidate block chosen while the VTC package was never requested
metrics.basis: r3 critique: the package is obtainable before the 3 Nov Q&A. Opened r3: the competition page lists the item under the Brief, and its 'Download brief' links open a modal asking for an email address to receive a download link; the page does not say the modal delivers the site package. A team member must request it with their own email (not done by this agent).

metrics.name: Result robustness class
metrics.good: ROBUST PASS: at most the noise floor at nominal and at every perturbation (north +/- tolerance, geometry +/- tolerance). ROBUST FAIL: above the floor at nominal and at every perturbation
metrics.bad: INDETERMINATE: the result changes sign inside the perturbation band, or exceeds a zero floor only by slivers; report the band, do not claim compliance
metrics.basis: r2 critique; the City tolerance for new shadow is unknown. Perturbation set (north +/-1 degree from P02-M01; geometry +/-0.5 m in plan and +/-1 m in height) is an editable team preset. r3: noise floor now derives from cell area, capped at 0.5% of the space area, and is 0 for 'no shadow' rules.
metrics.method: Re-run the forward test at each perturbation (5-9 runs); rerun envelope at the unfavourable north and keep the lower height.

metrics.name: Rule-set version gate
metrics.good: Every PolicyResult and board export prints rule-set version, source-document date and effective date; a 13 Nov release check compares the posted CDDG solar text with the July 2026 text
metrics.bad: Results without a version stamp, or run after 27 Oct 2026 against an unchecked rule set
metrics.basis: CDDG page (re-opened r3 on 21 Oct 2026) says final guidelines will be posted soon and take effect 27 Oct 2026; UDI does not say whether the downtown solar PDF continues. Process rule from the r2 critique.

metrics.name: Evidence gate and release mode
metrics.good: COMPLIANCE mode (PASS/FAIL badges) only if a team member opened the primary PDF and logged page numbers, cover date and SHA-256, a second reader confirmed Table 1, and each rule's evidence is verified or verified_secondary. Otherwise EXPLORATION mode: shadow areas and sweeps, no badge, watermark 'relay reading of an unopened guideline'
metrics.bad: 'verified' or a badge set from a relayed or draft-only reading: the data build fails
metrics.basis: Course requirement for honest source status (r2); r3 gate: no team member has opened the PDF, the 23 July 2025 report (cfsc1.pdf) or the 17 Sept 2025 report, memo and presentation (S59, S60, links seen, PDFs not opened). Evidence values: verified, verified_secondary, draft_only, unverified, team_assumption; badge colour comes from evidence, the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour from history; a schema test fails if status implies more confidence than evidence.

metrics.name: Table-1 class completeness
metrics.good: Every protected space carries a hand-checked Table-1 class keyed to the page-5 table; Park Board classification is never used to derive the class
metrics.bad: A space without a Table-1 class: the data build fails
metrics.basis: City open data (S47) classes Art Phillips Park, Cathedral Square and Victory Square as 'Urban Plaza', which would route them to the 3.2.1 minimise rule and drop the s.4.3 cenotaph rule; Jack Poole Plaza and Robson Square are absent.

metrics.name: Proposal height above SolarEnvelope
metrics.good: 0 m everywhere, consistent with a robust PASS (consistency check, tolerance 0.5 m)
metrics.bad: Above 0: name the governing space, clause and instant. An envelope built from the 4 Basic instants alone is not a valid reference
metrics.basis: Internal consistency test between forward test and envelope; the envelope is a 'new-shadow envelope' (protected polygon minus baseline shadow, receiver at its real elevation), unlike the classical solar envelope that allows no shadow beyond the lot (Knowles and Berry 1980). r3: built from the continuous azimuth-indexed sun table; 4 instants leave 33-39 degree azimuth gaps and over-state the allowable height.
metrics.method: For each cell c and receiver sample p unshaded in the baseline at the matching time: h = z_p + |c - p| x tan(altitude at the azimuth of p to c); take the minimum over p.

metrics.name: Non-residential floor-area capacity under the envelope vs 9.0 FSR
metrics.good: Capacity of the envelope-limited massing for office, commercial and other high-employment uses at least 9.0 x site area (about 103,200 m2 for 11,468 m2); shown beside the compliant height
metrics.bad: Capacity below the minimum: the compliant massing cannot meet the brief, so a deliberate breach, a different block or a different form must be argued
metrics.basis: The 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum is a brief fact supplied with the project; the PDF was not opened in r3. Site area from 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2 is approximate (260 x 475 ft = 11,474 m2).
metrics.method: Floors below the envelope height times plate area per use tag, divided by site area.

modules.method: 1) Load the versioned Table-1 GeoJSON; refuse files lacking version, Table-1 class or per-rule evidence. 2) Build three scenarios on terrain (existing plus approved; plus known proposed; plus proposal); extent = site disc plus receiver sun wedges; exclude trees and shade structures. 3) Take each rule's SweepWindow in UTC. 4) Per convex part and consecutive instant pair, hull the shadow polygons; cast onto terrain and each space at its elevation. 5) New shadow = proposal minus baseline, clipped to property lines or north sidewalk; list slivers separately. 6) Re-run at north and geometry tolerances; emit PASS, FAIL or INDETERMINATE only in COMPLIANCE mode, else EXPLORATION areas. 7) Coverage % from the N instants. 8) Envelope: for each cell and unshaded receiver sample take h = z_p + d x tan(altitude at azimuth p to cell); minimum over p; log governing space and instant. 9) Sweep tower position and rotation; stamp rule-set version.
visualization: Plan view on terrain: baseline shadow in grey, new shadow in red hatch, the swept-window band as a lighter red envelope around instants, protected polygons outlined by class colour; hour slider with 15-min ticks and the 4 Basic ticks marked 'format'; noise-floor slivers as thin dotted outlines; diagonal watermark 'EXPLORATION - relay reading of an unopened guideline' while the gate is closed

Per-space result card: PASS / FAIL / INDETERMINATE badge (COMPLIANCE mode only; INDETERMINATE hatched amber), 'EXPLORATION m2' otherwise, 'MINIMISE - report' for plazas and miniparks; each linked to clause, rule-set version and evidence level; badge colour from evidence (verified green, verified_secondary blue, draft_only orange, unverified grey hatched, team_assumption amber); FALSE ASSUMPTION special colour from history
Table of m2 of new shadow by space and window with the perturbation min-max in an extra column; bar of Shadow Coverage % for existing, proposed-additional and cumulative series

SolarEnvelope: translucent mesh over the site coloured by governing space, 20 m height contours, a section cut, proposal massing overlaid with over-envelope parts in red; tower-position sweep as a heat map of maximum compliant height per tower centre at a chosen rotation, with the 9.0 FSR capacity contour

3D elevation-aware view of receiver levels versus site level; shadow-reach rings (0.6 km, 1.4 km) and each space's sun wedge on a map, wedges hatched where the baseline relies on 2009 footprints, labelled 'new shadow overstated'
Block-sensitivity table: Basic-study result per candidate block

Board shadow sheet (A2 landscape, each board at most 10 MB, no identifying information): plan at a stated scale with a true-north arrow and scale bar, the 4 Basic instants labelled with local time and UTC offset, existing shadow grey and new shadow red, protected spaces outlined, legend with rule-set version, evidence level and mode

modules.human_judgment: Whether to meet the rule, seek an exception, or breach it deliberately and argue public benefit (the brief says justified breaches may be rewarded); where the hypothetical block sits and which alternatives count; correct classification of each space; which clock reading and which basis (total or new) of the cenotaph rule to follow, confirmed in writing by the City; which known proposed developments count; culturally significant spaces not in Table 1 (for example Indigenous gathering or ceremonial space proposed on site) that deserve sun although no rule protects them; trade-off against height and the 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum.

modules.name: Public-realm sun-hours map
modules.design_question: How many hours of direct sun reach the plaza, sidewalks, mid-block connections and transit plaza on key dates, and which massing moves recover sun?
modules.effort: M: about 5-6 dev-days (r2 adds altitude cut-off, horizon mask and probable-sun output, about 1 more; r3 adds EPW time alignment, under 0.5); four-date small multiples deferred past 13 Nov
inputs: SunVectorSet (explicit UTC), NorthFrame and SitePlacement from P02-M01
Proposed massing and context massing on the terrain mesh, context sized to the cut-off radius measured from the sensor area
Public-realm polygons from Layer 0 tags (public, retail frontage, transit plaza, mid-block links)
Grid spacing, sensor offset and time step settings
Minimum solar altitude (default 10 degrees, editable) and optional far-horizon profile (PVGIS printhorizon)
Optional EPW file for probable-sun hours (hour-ending records, converted to UTC by the header zone)

parameters.name: Study date
parameters.relationship: Winter noon shadows are about 3.2 times height (21 Dec, NOAA recomputation), reaching far beyond the block, so December sun on plazas is set largely by neighbouring towers; summer noon shadows (about 0.5 times height) stay local.

parameters.name: Position of tall mass relative to public space
parameters.relationship: Midday shadows fall north: a tower north of a plaza leaves it sunlit, one south of it shades it. East vs west only trades morning for afternoon sun (symmetric about 13:05 UTC-7 on 22 Sept); choose by use (geometry).

parameters.name: Podium height and setback
parameters.relationship: Higher street wall puts a wider shadow band over the sidewalk and ground-floor retail; a stepped podium on the sunny side reduces it (geometry). Plaza and sidewalk edges face NE/SE/SW/NW on this grid.

parameters.name: Sensor grid spacing
parameters.relationship: Finer spacing resolves shadow edges; cost grows with the inverse square of spacing (derived). Default 1 m is a team preset.

parameters.name: Sensor offset above ground
parameters.relationship: Offset 0 (the DirectSunStudy default) risks self-intersection with the ground mesh; use 0.05-0.1 m (team preset). SVF in P02-M08 uses 1.5 m because it describes the pedestrian view of the sky.

parameters.name: Time step
parameters.relationship: Sun hours equal sunlit samples divided by steps per hour, so a point's error is up to one time step; use 4 steps per hour for final figures (team preset).

parameters.name: Context radius
parameters.relationship: Shadow reach is H / tan(altitude): 3.2 times height at 21 Dec noon, 4.8 at 10:00, 9.6 at 09:00 (UTC-8). Radius = H / tan(cut-off), measured from the edge of the sensor area, not the site centre: 1.7 km for 300 m at 10 degrees, 3.4 km at 5.

parameters.name: Minimum solar altitude (cut-off)
parameters.relationship: Below the cut-off sun is counted as not assessed: on 21 Dec the sun is above 10 degrees for only about 5.0 of 8.2 daylight hours. A higher cut-off shrinks the context needed but drops real low-sun hours (team preset).

parameters.name: Far-horizon mask
parameters.relationship: A far-horizon mask from the PVGIS profile (about 10 degrees NE to SE, 7 N, near 0 S to W; coarse DEM bins) blocks winter-morning sun below it, so it cuts sun hours beyond what the context massing shows.

parameters.name: Weather availability and EPW time alignment
parameters.relationship: Counting a step only when EPW direct normal irradiance is at least 120 W/m2 (WMO sunshine threshold) gives probable sun hours. EPW hour h covers (h-1, h] in file time: convert by the header zone, use the midpoint sun vector.

metrics.name: Share of each public open space with at least 2 h direct sun on 21 March (whole day, cut-off 0), UK comparison
metrics.good: At least 50% of the area receives at least 2 h
metrics.bad: Less than 50% of the area receives 2 h
metrics.basis: BRE BR 209 amenity-area criterion recalled, not opened; written for UK housing amenity space, not a Vancouver requirement. Computed over sunrise-sunset on 21 March (altitude cut-off 0, labelled), not 10:00-16:00 on 22 Sept.
metrics.method: Sum of sunlit time steps per sensor on 21 March, then area-weighted share of sensors with at least 2 h.

metrics.name: Change in sun hours vs baseline (existing plus approved), design exploration on four dates
metrics.good: Descriptive only: report the area-weighted change and the sensors that lose sun; no pass/fail badge
metrics.bad: None: a zero-loss rule is stricter than any cited practice and would flag almost any CBD tower
metrics.basis: v1 called a zero-loss rule a verified City criterion; r1 made it an editable preset; r2 removes the bad badge and offers the relative test below. The City test covers only Table-1 spaces on 22 Sept 10:00-16:00 (see P02-M02).
metrics.method: Delta grid = proposal minus baseline sun hours per date; descriptive, separate from the policy test.

metrics.name: Relative sun-hours retention vs baseline (UK-style comparison)
metrics.good: At least 0.8 of the former value for an area that fails the 2 h / 50% test
metrics.bad: Below 0.8
metrics.basis: Recalled from BRE BR 209 practice by the packet and the r2 critic; BR 209 not opened; UK housing amenity practice, not a Vancouver requirement. Offered as a labelled comparison, no policy badge.
metrics.method: Ratio of per-space area-weighted sun hours, proposal over baseline, on 21 March.

metrics.name: Context radius and altitude cut-off printed on every output
metrics.good: Radius at least H_max / tan(cut-off) measured from the sensor area (about 1.7 km for 305 m at 10 degrees, derived); cut-off, horizon mask on/off and radius shown on the legend
metrics.bad: A fixed 1 km radius with whole-day low-sun hours, a radius measured from the site centre instead of the sensors, or an unlabelled cut-off
metrics.basis: r1 said about 1 km captures winter shadows; that holds only at winter noon (L/H 3.2). NOAA recomputation: 4.8 at 10:00 and 9.6 at 09:00 on 21 Dec (UTC-8), 3.4 at 09:00 on 21 Mar (UTC-7). The 10-degree default is a team preset; no sourced cut-off exists.
metrics.method: Derive radius from the cut-off; compare results at cut-offs 5, 10 and 15 degrees to show sensitivity.

modules.method: 1) Build a sensor mesh on the public-realm ground plane (1 m grid, offset 0.05-0.1 m) on the terrain mesh. 2) For each date (22 Sept 10:00-16:00, 21 Mar, 21 Jun, 21 Dec) take sun vectors at 4 steps per hour from P02-M01; drop vectors below the altitude cut-off (default 10 degrees) or below the far-horizon profile and count them as not assessed. 3) Size the context to H_max / tan(cut-off) around the sensor area. 4) Cast each reversed vector from every sensor through proposal plus context (sun hours = row sum of the intersection matrix / steps per hour); repeat for the baseline. 5) Optionally keep only steps with EPW direct normal irradiance of at least 120 W/m2 (probable hours), aligning EPW hours to interval midpoints in UTC. 6) Report hours per sensor, area share at or above the preset hours, delta and retention ratio vs baseline. 7) Colour the mesh with the Ecotect set, 0-12 h. three.js shadow maps: preview only.
visualization: False-colour mesh on the ground plane, 0-12 h legend with 2 h contour lines; dotted overlay on sensors whose sun is removed by the horizon mask
Small multiples for the four dates (after 13 Nov)
Delta map: blue = sun gained, red = sun lost vs baseline, labelled 'design exploration, not the City test', no pass/fail badge
Bar chart: percent of each space with at least 2 h on 21 Mar, with source and 'UK, unverified' printed on the bar; second bar for the retention ratio
Paired maps: geometric hours vs probable hours (EPW direct normal at least 120 W/m2)
Legend footer printing altitude cut-off, horizon mask on/off and context radius; time-slider shadow animation (preview only)
outputs: SunHoursGrid {mesh, hours[], not_assessed_hours[], cutoff_deg, horizon_mask, context_radius_m} per date
ProbableSunHoursGrid per date (EPW-weighted)
AreaShareTable {space_id, share_ge_threshold}
DeltaGrid and RetentionGrid vs baseline
Per-point sun/shade flags by hour (feeds wind/thermal-comfort and public-realm modules)
modules.human_judgment: Which spaces deserve sun (retail high-street sidewalk, transit plaza, cultural or ceremonial space) and how much; morning versus afternoon preference by programme (cafe terrace vs quiet shaded seating); Indigenous and 'City in Nature' planting and gathering needs; the cut-off and whether to apply the horizon mask.
modules.limits: Direct sun only; Vancouver winters are mostly overcast, so geometric hours overstate winter conditions and probable hours rest on one typical year. The cut-off and far-horizon mask are presets. Trees, canopies and temporary structures are ignored. Geometry is static. The 2-hour threshold is UK practice and unverified; the City test lives in P02-M02. No comfort model.

modules.name: Facade and roof solar radiation and PV potential
modules.design_question: How much solar radiation reaches each facade and roof surface once neighbours are included, and where does PV or shading pay off on a grid rotated 45 degrees?
modules.effort: M: about 5-7 dev-days (r2: about 1 more for horizon mask and PVGIS conversions; r3 EPW alignment under 0.5)
inputs: Proposed massing with surface types (roof, wall) from Layer 0
Context massing on the terrain mesh
Weather file (CWEC 2020 or TMYx EPW, hour-ending records converted to UTC by the header zone) and NorthFrame from P02-M01
Optional: PVGIS horizon profile as a sky mask; window-to-wall ratio, PV coverage and efficiency presets (Advanced mode)

parameters.name: Surface orientation and tilt (true azimuth)
parameters.relationship: PVGIS-ERA5 vertical walls, kWh/m2/yr, default horizon (no-horizon in brackets): S 1,072 (1,091); SW 1,045 (1,046); SE 955 (1,008); W 809 (809); E 688 (753); NW 459 (459); NE 388 (429); N 242 (252). Roof 1,245 (1,253).

parameters.name: Context obstruction
parameters.relationship: More and closer obstructing towers cut direct and sky-diffuse radiation on lower floors; upper-tower and roof surfaces approach the unobstructed values (geometry).

parameters.name: Reflectance (ground and facades)
parameters.relationship: Higher albedo raises radiation on vertical surfaces (pvlib default 0.25). RadiationStudy has no inter-reflections except a ground hemisphere: conservative for PV yield, but non-conservative for overheating loads (P02-M05) where neighbours are glass.

parameters.name: Weather file and time alignment
parameters.relationship: Annual totals scale with the file; CWEC 2020 and TMYx exist for Vancouver. EPW hours are hour-ending in file time: convert to UTC by the header zone before pairing with sun vectors. Comparing unobstructed values with PVGIS exposes file or north-angle errors.

parameters.name: PV efficiency and coverage ratio
parameters.relationship: Yield = irradiation x efficiency x performance ratio x covered area. PVGIS 1 kWp, 14% loss, building-integrated, no horizon, kWh/kWp/yr: roof 953; S 835; SW 800; SE 772; W 605; E 565; NW 323; NE 301; N 155.

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio
parameters.relationship: Radiation is computed on the whole envelope; PV-usable area is roughly (1 minus WWR) times face area times coverage, so higher WWR reduces BIPV area and raises solar gain (see P02-M05).

parameters.name: PVGIS aspect and mounting convention
parameters.relationship: PVGIS aspect: 0 = south, 90 = west, -90 = east, so aspect = true azimuth - 180 (SW 225 gives 45); a wrong sign swaps SW and SE. Building-integrated yields 1.6% (NE) to 2.8% (SW) less than free-standing.

parameters.name: Far horizon in the reference
parameters.relationship: PVGIS DEM horizon lowers E by 9%, NE by 10%, SE by 5% and S by 2% versus no horizon; a Radiance run without a far horizon must be compared with usehorizon=0, or mask both with the PVGIS profile.

metrics.name: Solar access ratio per face
metrics.unit: % of unobstructed irradiation at the face's own azimuth
metrics.good: At least 80%
metrics.bad: Below 50%
metrics.basis: Editable preset. Reference is a PVGIS azimuth curve (15-degree bins), not four cardinal values; PVGIS values verified (r2 added no-horizon values), cut-offs unsourced. Compagnon 2004 recalled, not opened.
metrics.method: Face irradiation from the radiation study divided by the PVGIS value for the face azimuth (tilt 90) or the roof (tilt 0) with the same horizon setting, interpolated between bins.

metrics.name: PV specific yield on candidate faces
metrics.good: At least 700 (editable): unobstructed building-integrated SW (800), SE (772) and roof (953) reach it; W (605), E (565), NW (323) and NE (301) never do
metrics.bad: Below 420 (about half the 835 south-wall reference)
metrics.basis: v1 good cut-off of 843 equals a due-south wall, which a street-aligned tower on a 45-degree grid does not have, so no face could pass. Reference yields are verified PVGIS outputs (r2: building-integrated, no horizon); the cut-offs are team presets.

metrics.name: Simulated unobstructed irradiation vs PVGIS reference
metrics.good: Within plus or minus 10% of the PVGIS value with the same horizon setting and azimuth conversion
metrics.bad: Beyond plus or minus 20%: check weather file, north angle, aspect sign or horizon setting
metrics.basis: QA tolerance chosen by team; ERA5 bias was not assessed. r2: the DEM horizon alone moves NE by 10%, so an unlike-for-like comparison would breach the good band.
metrics.method: Unit-test aspect = azimuth - 180 against SW 823.5 and NE 306.3 kWh/kWp (free-standing, no horizon).

modules.method: 1) Sub-divide facade and roof faces into a sensor mesh. 2) Build a cumulative sky matrix from the EPW (Perez-type sky, Reinhart patches), with hour-ending records converted to UTC and sun at interval midpoints; rotate it by the NorthFrame; optionally block patches below the PVGIS horizon profile. 3) Run the radiation study: intersect sensor rays with context geometry on terrain to get visible sky and ground; add direct, diffuse and ground-reflected terms; output kWh/m2 and W/m2 (no inter-reflections). 4) Divide each face value by the PVGIS value at the face's own azimuth (aspect = azimuth - 180, same horizon setting) to get the solar access ratio. 5) Estimate PV yield with pvlib transposition (Perez or Hay-Davies) and a performance ratio; for building-integrated faces use the building-mounted references. 6) State the bias per downstream use: conservative for PV yield, non-conservative for overheating (see P02-M05). 7) Print thresholds and their status beside each result.
visualization: False-colour mesh on the massing, kWh/m2/yr legend with tick marks at the PVGIS unobstructed values for N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW walls and the roof (toggle: horizon on/off)
Azimuth curve chart: PVGIS reference line (15-degree bins) with each face plotted at its true azimuth
Radiation rose or dome for a selected surface; monthly bar chart per selected face
Per-face table with solar access ratio badge showing threshold status (team assumption)
outputs: IrradianceMesh {face_id, kWh_m2_yr, W_m2 hourly}
SolarAccessRatio per face
PV_kWh_by_face
Hourly irradiance on glazing (feeds P02-M05, energy and carbon, MEP and facade modules)
modules.human_judgment: Whether facade PV or BIPV suits the design and cultural intent (the jury penalises generic design); trade-offs with views, daylight and expression; acceptable payback.
modules.limits: No inter-reflections, so reflective glass neighbours are ignored: conservative for PV yield, non-conservative for overheating loads. Weather files are typical years. PVGIS-ERA5 values are satellite-reanalysis and its DEM horizon is coarse; the reference is unvalidated here. Facade PV thresholds are team presets. Cost, tree shading, snow and soiling are not modelled.

modules.name: Solar gain and overheating screening
modules.design_question: Which facades and floors carry the highest warm-season solar load on glazing, how does shading change heating-season gain, and what does that mean for TEDI?
modules.effort: M: about 5-7 dev-days for screening; thermal model is a separate packet
inputs: Hourly irradiance on facades from P02-M04 (EPW hours aligned to UTC midpoints)
Window-to-wall ratio by orientation and floor (Layer 0 or Advanced presets)
Glazing SHGC and VT presets (Advanced mode)
Program tags (office, residential, hotel) and weather file, including future-climate file
Optional multi-bounce irradiance for floors facing glazed neighbours

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio by orientation
parameters.relationship: Solar load on glazing scales with glazed area times irradiation times SHGC, so raising WWR on west-facing walls (SW, NW on this grid) raises peak load roughly in proportion (physics).

parameters.name: Facade orientation
parameters.relationship: West vertical gets about 17% more annual irradiation than east with the PVGIS DEM horizon (809 vs 688 kWh/m2/yr) but only 7% with none (809 vs 753); on this grid SW 1,045 vs NW 459 and SE 955 vs NE 388 (default horizon).

parameters.name: Shading projection (overhang and fin angles)
parameters.relationship: Larger overhang or fin projection masks more of the sky dome seen by the glazing and lowers direct gain; Ladybug Sky Mask accepts overhang and fin projection angles for a chosen orientation.

parameters.name: Program and internal gains
parameters.relationship: Program sets internal gains and occupancy hours, so identical solar load has different overheating consequences for hotel, residential and office floors; values come from Advanced-mode presets, not sourced here.

parameters.name: Climate scenario
parameters.relationship: Typical-year files understate future warm-season hours; Canadian future-climate files are listed on Climate.OneBuilding (2022 set), allowing present vs future comparison.

parameters.name: Heating-season (Oct-Apr) useful gain
parameters.relationship: Winter glazing gain offsets heating demand and so lowers TEDI; shading that cuts June-September load also cuts October-April gain, so the best shading is orientation-specific (physics; TEDI target from HBP s.2.2).

parameters.name: Reflected gain from glazed neighbours
parameters.relationship: Reflections from glass neighbours raise glazing load on lower floors, which P02-M04 omits; an optional multi-bounce Radiance run (ambient bounces above 0) adds an allowance for floors facing glazed neighbours (physics).

metrics.name: Warm-season (Jun-Sep) irradiation on glazing by facade
metrics.good: At or below the building-wide mean
metrics.bad: More than 1.25 times the building-wide mean
metrics.basis: Relative ranking preset for screening; no sourced Vancouver threshold.

metrics.name: Thermal energy demand intensity (TEDI), needs a thermal model
metrics.good: At most 15 on the non-Passive-House route (HBP s.2.2), with TEUI/GHGI targets by use and a low-carbon energy connection
metrics.bad: Above 15 without Passive House certification
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Higher Buildings Policy (amended 31 Mar 2026) s.2.2 as read by the round-1 reviewer (relay; PDF not opened by the team); by-use TEUI/GHGI values not transcribed; City Energy Modelling Guidelines returned HTTP 403.

metrics.name: Hours of exceedance of the adaptive comfort threshold (UK comparison, needs thermal model)
metrics.good: 3% or less
metrics.bad: More than 3%
metrics.basis: CIBSE TM52 (2013) exists, but its criteria were not displayed on the opened page; the 3% value is recalled. Vancouver's overheating limit (Passive House overheating frequency; City Energy Modelling Guidelines comfort limit) was not opened: the Passive House Institute page lists no numbers.

modules.method: 1) Take hourly irradiance on each facade face from P02-M04; for floors facing glazed neighbours optionally rerun with ambient bounces above 0. 2) Multiply by glazed fraction and SHGC (and a sky-mask shading factor when overhangs or fins are set) to get solar load on glazing in W/m2 of facade. 3) Aggregate to warm-season (Jun-Sep) kWh/m2 and peak hourly load per orientation and floor band, plus heating-season (Oct-Apr) useful gain. 4) Rank facades against the building mean. 5) Export loads to an EnergyPlus-class model to get TEDI against the HBP s.2.2 target and hours of exceedance against the adopted overheating criterion (to be confirmed). 6) Repeat with a future-climate file.
visualization: Unfolded facade elevation heat-map (W/m2) by orientation and floor band
Polar chart of warm-season load by azimuth, with heating-season gain as a second ring
Stereographic sky-mask diagram showing overhang or fin effect at a selected window
Present vs future-climate bar pair
outputs: SolarLoadByFace {face_id, W_m2_peak, kWh_m2_warm_season, kWh_m2_heating_season}
ShadingEffectiveness (percent load reduction, and percent heating-season gain lost)
OverheatingRiskFlag per facade band (feeds energy, MEP cooling and facade/material modules)
modules.human_judgment: Acceptable overheating risk; passive vs mechanical cooling; facade expression versus shading; trade-off between summer shading, winter gain, daylight and views; Passive House versus TEDI route.
modules.limits: Screening only: no thermal mass, ventilation, blinds or occupant behaviour. The Passive House overheating criterion and the City Energy Modelling Guidelines comfort limit were not opened; TM52 is a UK comparison only. Weather and future files are scenarios, not forecasts. Glazing properties are presets until Advanced mode is filled. TEDI needs a thermal model outside this packet.

modules.name: Floor-plate depth-to-window daylight screen
modules.design_question: Which parts of each tower floor plate lie beyond practical daylight reach of the facade, by programme, before any simulation is run?
inputs: Floor-plate polygons per level and core footprint (Layer 0)
Facade lines with window-to-wall ratio and head height (Layer 0 or Advanced presets)
Programme tags per area (office, residential, hotel, core, mechanical)
Obstruction angle from context massing (optional)

parameters.name: Plate depth (window to core or far window)
parameters.relationship: Deeper plates leave a larger share of floor area beyond daylight reach (geometry); with a fixed core, widening the plate deepens the daylit band instead.

parameters.name: Window head height
parameters.relationship: Higher head height pushes daylight further in. Candidate sources: ASHRAE 90.1 sidelit zones (1 and 2 times head height) and the BRE/BS 8206-2 limiting-depth rule, both recalled, not opened; k = 2.0 stays a team assumption.

parameters.name: Glazing visual transmittance (VT)
parameters.relationship: VT below 0.4 can halve or more of the incoming light; VT above about 0.6 can cause glare, so VT trades daylight against glare.

parameters.name: Neighbour obstruction angle
parameters.relationship: A tall neighbour close to the facade raises the obstruction angle and lowers sky visible from lower-floor windows, shortening reach; upper floors recover (geometry).

parameters.name: Programme tag
parameters.relationship: Only regularly occupied programme (office, residential, hotel rooms) counts in the denominator; cores, mechanical and back-of-house are excluded, so the tagging in Layer 0 changes the result.

metrics.name: Share of regularly occupied area within daylight reach
metrics.good: At least 75%
metrics.bad: Below 40%
metrics.basis: Geometric proxy borrowing LEED sDA tiers (75% three credits, 55% two, 40% one) from the open-source LEED v4.1 implementation; reach factor k = 2.0 is unsourced.
metrics.method: Area of occupied polygon within k x head height of a window line divided by occupied area.

metrics.name: Average daylight factor of a typical room
metrics.good: Above 5% (well lit)
metrics.bad: Below 2% (artificial light needed throughout)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] CIBSE Lighting Guide 10 (1999) bands quoted via Wikipedia. Overcast-sky metric, not climate-based; UK practice is reported to have moved to EN 17037 illuminance targets (BR 209, 2022; not opened), so prefer P02-M07.
metrics.method: Split-flux style estimate from glazed area, VT, obstruction angle, surface reflectance and room area.

metrics.name: Limiting room depth (second check)
metrics.good: L/W + L/H at or below 2/(1 - Rb), with Rb the mean reflectance of the rear half of the room
metrics.bad: Above that limit: room too deep for sidelighting alone
metrics.basis: BRE / BS 8206-2 limiting-depth formula recalled, not opened; offered as an optional second check beside the team-assumption reach factor.

modules.method: 1) For each typical floor (lower, mid, upper) take occupied polygons by programme tag. 2) Build window lines from facade segments with WWR and head height. 3) Compute distance from each point (0.5 m grid) to the nearest window line; label facade orientation from the NorthFrame (street faces are NE/SE/SW/NW). 4) Daylight reach = k x head height (k = 2.0 preset; k = 1 and 2 mirror ASHRAE-style primary and secondary zones, to verify). 5) Share of occupied area within reach per programme. 6) Optional second check: limiting room depth L/W + L/H <= 2/(1 - Rb) (recalled). 7) Flag floors below the proxy thresholds and recommend running P02-M07.
visualization: Floor-plan heat-map of distance to nearest window (m) with the reach contour for k = 1 and k = 2
Lower, mid and upper typical plates side by side
Section sketch showing a daylight reach cone
Stacked bar of percent area within reach by programme
outputs: DaylightReachMask per floor
AreaShareByProgramme
Rooms flagged below proxy thresholds (feed P02-M07, programme, structure and core-position modules)
modules.human_judgment: Where to put cores, services and non-daylit programme; acceptable depth for offices versus residential bedrooms; use of light wells, atria or double-height public floors; occupant wellbeing beyond the metric.
modules.limits: Geometric proxy only. Ignores glazing, neighbours (unless an obstruction angle is supplied), blinds and climate. The reach multiplier and limiting-depth formula are recalled, not opened. Daylight factor assumes an overcast sky and is not climate-based. Vancouver Building By-law window rules were not checked.

modules.name: Interior daylight (sDA, ASE, EN 17037)
modules.design_question: Do representative floors reach sDA, ASE and EN 17037 daylight targets once neighbours, glazing, operable shades and plate depth are included?
modules.effort: L: about 10-14 dev-days (server-side Radiance pipeline with aperture groups and shade states)
inputs: Representative floors (lower, mid, upper): plate, facade WWR, glazing VT, head height (Advanced presets)
Interior reflectances and shading devices with shade transmittance (default 0.05)
Context massing and NorthFrame from P02-M01
EPW file (CWEC 2020 or TMYx) and occupancy schedule (default 8:00-18:00 in file time; see clock-basis parameter)

parameters.name: Glazing visual transmittance
parameters.relationship: Higher VT raises sDA but also ASE and glare risk; VT below 0.4 can halve incoming light, above about 0.6 can cause glare.

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio
parameters.relationship: More glazing raises daylight at depth but increases ASE on the SW and NW facades of a street-aligned tower, and solar gain.

parameters.name: Plate depth
parameters.relationship: Deeper plate lowers sDA because points far from windows seldom reach 300 lux; the share of area at 300 lux for 50% of hours falls with distance (geometry plus simulation).

parameters.name: Neighbour obstruction by floor height
parameters.relationship: Lower floors see more obstruction from neighbouring towers; sDA rises with floor height above the context, so lower floors suit public or less daylight-dependent programme.

parameters.name: Occupied hours and sensor plane
parameters.relationship: Annual metrics depend on the schedule (default 8:00-18:00) and the plane: 0.762 m for LM-83, LEED and WELL IES routes; 0.85 m for EN 17037 (recalled, standard not opened). A longer schedule adds low-light hours and lowers sDA.

parameters.name: Shading devices and blinds
parameters.relationship: LEED v4.1 sDA is computed with an operable-shade schedule that keeps at most 2% of sensors at 1,000 lx or more direct sun (default shade transmittance 0.05); ASE is computed without blinds. Ignoring shades overstates sDA.

parameters.name: Clock basis of the schedule
parameters.relationship: EPW hour h covers (h-1, h] (hour-ending). BC has run on UTC-7 all year since 8 Mar 2026; EPW file time is, by recalled convention, local standard time (UTC-8), so an 8:00-18:00 wall-clock schedule is 7:00-17:00 in the file. Label schedules.

metrics.name: sDA 300 lx / 50% of hours with operable shades (LEED v4.1 Option 1)
metrics.good: At least 75% (3 credits), 55% (2), 40% (1), with a shade schedule keeping at most 2% of sensors at 1,000 lx direct; an extra credit or 'Exemplary performance' if every space reaches 55%
metrics.bad: Below 40%, or no shade schedule can comply: 0 credits
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] v1 computed sDA without shades. leed.py (opened) uses a shade schedule with the 2% rule and awards 0 credits if it cannot comply. USGBC and IES LM-83-12 texts not opened.
metrics.method: Run leed_option_one as published; report sDA with shades, blinds-up and blinds-down variants, and the per-space 55% check.

metrics.name: Annual sunlight exposure ASE 1000 lx / 250 h (no blinds)
metrics.good: 10% or less
metrics.bad: More than 10%: written glare-control note needed
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Open-source LEED v4.1 code (sensor fails ASE at 250 or more occupied hours above 1,000 lx direct; above 10% of area adds a note); IES LM-83 and LEED texts not opened.
metrics.method: Sensors receiving direct illuminance of at least 1,000 lx for 250 h or more, as a share of area.

metrics.name: EN 17037 target and minimum illuminance
metrics.unit: lx over % area for 50% of daylight hours
metrics.good: Target 300 / 500 / 750 lx (minimum / medium / high) over at least 50% of area; minimum 100 / 300 / 500 lx over 95%
metrics.bad: Fails the minimum tier at any level
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Open-source en17037.py (opened; 4,380 daylight hours = the half-year with most daylight); CEN standard not opened; sunlight-exposure and view criteria not modelled; reference plane 0.85 m recalled.

metrics.name: WELL v2 L06 daylight optimisation (IES route)
metrics.good: sDA 300/50% at least 55% (tier 1) or at least 75% (tier 2)
metrics.bad: Below 55%
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Values hard-coded in well.py (label WELL v2 Q2 2025, opened); WELL text not opened. EN 17037 route also exists in the code.

metrics.name: WELL v2 L01 light exposure and education (IES route, daylight part)
metrics.good: sDA 150 lx / 50% of hours over at least 30% of area
metrics.bad: Below 30%
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Values in well.py (opened); WELL text not opened.

modules.method: 1) Build a Radiance model per representative floor: plate, facade, glazing VT, reflectances, aperture groups with operable shades (transmittance 0.05), context massing rotated by the NorthFrame. 2) Create an annual sky matrix from the EPW (Reinhart subdivision), aligning hour-ending records to UTC midpoints. 3) Place sensors at 0.762 m (LM-83, LEED, WELL IES route) and 0.85 m (EN 17037). 4) Run the matrix-based annual daylight recipe for hourly illuminance. 5) Post-process with leed_option_one and the WELL post-processors as published: sDA 300 lx/50% with the 2% direct-sun shade schedule, blinds-up and blinds-down variants, ASE 1000 lx/250 h, EN 17037 tiers (4,380 daylight hours), WELL L01 and L06. 6) Summarise per floor, programme and orientation, area-weighted. Run server-side; cache per floor.
visualization: Floor-plan false-colour map of daylight autonomy (0-100%) with the 50% contour
ASE map (hours above 1000 lx, 0-1000 h legend, 250 h contour)
Badges for LEED credit tier, EN 17037 tier and WELL tier linked to the threshold source and its status
Shade-feasibility panel: hours the 2% rule forces shades down, per floor
Floor-by-floor bar chart of sDA and ASE; facade overlay where direct sun exceeds the ASE limit
outputs: DaylightGrid {DA_pct, sDA_with_shades, sDA_blinds_up, ASE, EN17037_tier, WELL_L01, WELL_L06} per floor
BlindsFeasibility {complies, fail_hours}
Per-floor summary JSON (feeds programme net-lettable quality, lighting energy, facade and interior modules, and boards)
modules.human_judgment: Choice of representative floors and glazing strategy; accepting deep plates for public or cultural programme; balance of glare, views and privacy; whether residential-unit rules apply; qualitative spatial quality that the metrics do not capture.
modules.limits: Representative floors only. Typical-year weather. Partitions and furniture unknown at schematic design. LEED and WELL are rating systems, not Vancouver code; Vancouver Building By-law natural-light rules were not checked. Thresholds come from open-source code, not the primary standards. Heavy compute needs a server. ASE excludes blinds by design.

modules.name: Sky view, neighbour-facade exposure and reflected-sun screen
modules.design_question: How much open sky and direct sun do street-level points and neighbouring (or sibling) tower facades keep, and does the proposal's glazing reflect sun onto streets or neighbours?
modules.effort: M: about 5-7 dev-days for SVF and neighbour sun hours (r3 adds on-site sibling-tower exposure, under 1); reflected-sun screen is a roadmap sub-mode (about 3-4 more dev-days)
inputs: Proposed massing and context massing on the terrain mesh, context sized to the P02-M03 cut-off radius measured from the sample points
Sample points: ground grid in public realm (1.5 m); facade grid or window centres on neighbouring towers facing the site and, for multi-tower schemes, on the proposal's own towers
NorthFrame and SunVectorSet from P02-M01; altitude cut-off and optional horizon mask from P02-M03
Optional (roadmap): glazing specular reflectance and facade curvature (Advanced mode)

parameters.name: Tower height and podium setback
parameters.relationship: Street-level SVF falls as height-to-width of the street canyon rises; setting the tower back from the frontage above the podium raises sidewalk SVF (geometry).

parameters.name: Street, lane and mid-block link width
parameters.relationship: Narrow lanes and mid-block connections between tall faces have low SVF; widening or stepping the walls raises it (geometry).

parameters.name: Sample height and plane
parameters.relationship: Point-at-height evaluates sky exposure; a plane or oriented surface gives true sky view (fraction of sky seen from a surface), as defined in Ladybug Sky Mask. Ground SVF at 1.5 m is a team preset.

parameters.name: Patch density
parameters.relationship: Higher sky-patch subdivision raises accuracy and compute time; low density mis-estimates SVF near narrow gaps.

parameters.name: Tree canopy
parameters.relationship: Canopy lowers real SVF below the massing-only value; not modelled here, which overestimates SVF where trees exist (limit).

parameters.name: Neighbour facade position and proposal height
parameters.relationship: On 22 Sept shadows sweep NW through N to NE (306-52 degrees) up to about 590 m for 300 m of height, so neighbour facades facing the proposal on that side lose most direct sun; wider plates widen the lost band (geometry).

parameters.name: Altitude cut-off and context radius for 21 Dec
parameters.relationship: Neighbour-facade sun hours on 21 Dec use the P02-M03 altitude cut-off; at 10 degrees a 300 m tower needs about 1.7 km of context, measured from the facade points, not 1 km (derived).

parameters.name: On-site tower separation (multi-tower schemes)
parameters.relationship: A tower of height Ha shades height z on a sibling tower to its north when the separation is below (Ha - z) x cot(altitude); at the 22 Sept noon altitude of 40.8 degrees that is 1.16 m per metre (geometry). No Vancouver separation figure was opened.

parameters.name: Glazing reflectance and facade curvature (roadmap)
parameters.relationship: Higher specular reflectance and concave curvature raise reflected-beam intensity and can focus it; a concave glass tower at 20 Fenchurch Street focused sun onto streets in 2013 (precedent, not a threshold).

metrics.name: Street-level sky view factor (cosine-weighted)
metrics.good: Context markers only, no pass/fail: Local Climate Zone compact high-rise band (recalled about 0.2-0.4)
metrics.bad: Not used as a pass/fail: a 244-305 m CBD tower would mark almost every street bad
metrics.basis: LCZ values are classification descriptors, not performance targets (r1). Stewart and Oke 2012 not opened; WUDAPT pages show no numbers.

metrics.name: Change in SVF vs baseline context at mid-block links and transit plaza
metrics.good: No decrease
metrics.bad: Decrease of 0.1 or more
metrics.basis: Editable preset for design comparison; no sourced threshold. The only judged SVF metric.

metrics.name: Change in direct sun hours on neighbouring-tower facade points vs baseline (22 Sept, 21 Dec)
metrics.good: No loss at residential or hotel windows
metrics.bad: More than 20% loss of a point's sun hours on either date
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no sourced Vancouver or Canadian threshold for neighbour facades. The 20% cut-off resembles the UK relative test (at least 0.8 of former value; recalled, BR 209 not opened, UK practice). r2: 21 Dec hours exclude sun below the P02-M03 cut-off, reported separately. r3: the same metric is reported without a badge for sibling towers of the proposal.
metrics.method: DirectSunStudy-type intersection on facade points, proposal minus baseline.

metrics.name: Reflected-sun screen (roadmap)
metrics.good: No ground or facade receiver lies inside a specular beam from proposal glazing on any study date
metrics.bad: Any receiver hit, or concave or focusing glazing present
metrics.basis: Geometric screen only; no Vancouver or BC threshold for reflected irradiance or luminance was found.

modules.method: 1) Generate sample points: ground grid at 1.5 m on the public realm and a facade grid (window centres) on neighbouring towers and, for multi-tower schemes, on the proposal's own towers. 2) Build a sky dome (Tregenza or Reinhart patches) at each point. 3) Cast rays through proposal plus context on terrain; SVF is the cosine-weighted fraction of unobstructed patch solid angle (name the weighting). 4) Compute facade sun hours for 22 Sept and 21 Dec with DirectSunStudy logic, applying the P02-M03 cut-off and horizon mask, context radius measured from the points; report removed hours. 5) Output SVF and sun hours per point plus deltas against baseline. 6) Roadmap: mirror each sun vector in every glazed face and flag receivers inside the beam (screen only). 7) Draw fisheye sky masks with sun-path overlay; LB Sky Mask is the reference, UMEP SVF the raster cross-check.
visualization: False-colour SVF map on public ground (0-1 legend with Local Climate Zone band markers, labelled 'context only')
Fisheye (stereographic or equidistant) sky-mask diagrams at 3-5 chosen points with sun-path overlay
Delta SVF map vs baseline; histogram of SVF by public space
Elevation of each neighbouring and sibling tower coloured by sun-hour loss (blue = none, red = loss) for 22 Sept and 21 Dec; sibling towers labelled 'on-site, no badge'
Roadmap: plan and elevation with reflected-beam rays from glazed faces to hit receivers
outputs: SVFGrid {mesh, svf[], weighting}
SkyMask diagrams (SVG)
DeltaSVF (feeds wind/thermal comfort, public-realm and human-scale, daylight and board modules)
NeighbourFacadeSunGrid {facade_id, hours_baseline, hours_proposed, delta_h, retention_ratio, not_assessed_h}
OnSiteMutualExposure {tower_pair, separation_m, sibling_facade_sun_loss_h, svf_between}
ReflectedSunFlags (roadmap) {face_id, receiver_id, date, time}
modules.human_judgment: What degree of enclosure is desirable: intimate street vs open sky and mountain views; 'City in Nature' and cultural sightlines; whether low SVF in lanes is acceptable for character; how much neighbour sun loss is acceptable and for whom; tower-to-tower separation and mutual overlook in a multi-tower scheme; glazing choice versus reflection risk.
modules.limits: Geometric only: no trees, canopies or weather. The link between SVF and heat-island intensity or pedestrian comfort is climatological and not calibrated for Vancouver. LCZ bands are context markers, not targets. The reflected-sun screen has no glare threshold and ignores curvature focusing unless modelled. Accuracy depends on sky-patch density and on the altitude cut-off. No tower-separation rule was opened.
