sources.title: SunCalc
sources.extract: README re-read in r2. BSD-2-Clause. v2.0 is a precision-focused rewrite with breaking changes (not listed on the page): azimuth in degrees clockwise from north (0 N, 90 E, 180 S), altitude apparent (refraction-corrected) in degrees; sun accuracy about 0.08 degrees, built on Meeus and validated against JPL Horizons and USNO. v1.x returned radians from south. npm registry (opened r2) lists latest 2.1.1; the integrity hash begins sha512-ufMOPzYRk5aomEs3... sources.title: Knowles and Berry (1980), Solar envelope concepts: moderate density building applications
sources.extract: Opened in r2 (abstract). Proposes a 'solar zoning envelope': the largest building volume a parcel can hold without casting shadow on neighbouring properties at designated times; tested on Los Angeles sites. Wavefront OBJ (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavefront_.obj_file, opened): right-hand coordinate system, no up axis defined, no units. three.js DEFAULT_UP (0,1,0) (S29). Rhino, SketchUp, Revit and IFC are commonly Z-up (recalled, not opened). Derived: Y-up to Z-up needs a +90 degree rotation about X; a Y/Z swap has determinant -1.

sources.title: BC Gov News: Adopting permanent daylight saving time (and companion release on time zone code PCT)
sources.extract: Opened in r2; the r3 critic re-read it and agrees. Clocks moved ahead on Sunday 8 March 2026, 'the final time change'; most of BC, including the Pacific zone, stays on UTC-7 year-round; no change on 1 Nov 2026; legal basis the 2019 Interpretation Amendment Act, implemented by regulation; East Kootenay and Golden area keep switching with Alberta. Companion release 2026CITZ0009-001073 (archive.news.gov.bc.ca, opened, 17 Sept 2026): the year-round zone is called Pacific Time, code PCT; no clocks turned back on 1 Nov 2026; no guidance on software or tz identifiers.

sources.title: IANA tz database NEWS (release 2026b)
sources.extract: Opened in r2 and re-read in r3. 2026b (2026-04-22): British Columbia moved to permanent -07, legally on 2026-03-09; the data model it as occurring on 2026-11-01 at 02:00 as a temporary workaround for a limitation in CLDR 48.1 (2026-01-08); America/Vancouver and Canada/Pacific use the abbreviation MST; zic 2023d-2026a slim files may ignore the 1 Nov transition (use fat files via zic -b fat or a newer zic). Later releases 2026c (2026-07-08), 2026d (2026-09-11) and 2026e (2026-09-29) do not change Vancouver. The notes do not mention browsers, ICU or Java; that a browser's bundled tz data may predate 2026b is a derived risk, not a sourced fact.

sources.title: Sunshine duration (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Opened in r2. Sunshine duration is the period when direct solar irradiance exceeds a threshold of 120 W/m2 (WMO-linked definition; the WMO guide itself was not opened); relative sunshine is the share of daylight duration.

sources.extract: Opened in r3. flags.claim: About 1 km of context captures winter shadows of a 300 m tower (P02-M03 context radius; also reused by P02-M08 for 21 Dec and quoted in P02-M02)
flags.correction: Radius = H / tan(minimum solar altitude): about 1.7 km for 300 m at a 10-degree cut-off, 3.4 km at 5 degrees; print the cut-off on every output and optionally apply a far-horizon mask. For the policy windows use the lowest rule altitude: about 0.6 km on 22 Sept, about 1.4 km for 305 m if the 11 Nov wall-clock reading applies.
flags.detail: 1 km holds only at winter solar noon (L/H 3.2). NOAA-algorithm recomputation for 49.283 N, 123.12 W: 21 Dec 09:00 UTC-8 apparent altitude 6.0 degrees (L/H 9.6; the critique's geometric value 9.79), 10:00 11.7 degrees (L/H 4.8), 15:00 8.2 degrees (L/H 6.9-7.0); 21 Mar 09:00 PDT 16.4 degrees (L/H 3.4); 11 Nov 09:00 UTC-8 12.7 degrees (L/H 4.45). r3: reproduced independently (S62). Whole-day studies include these low-sun hours, so a 1 km context overstates sun hours wherever towers 1-3 km away block low sun.

The label is used loosely, so neither the label nor the tz abbreviation (tzdata 2026b prints MST for BC) can decide the offset on its own.

flags.claim: 11 Nov 2026 is PST (UTC-8) because daylight saving time ended on Sunday 1 Nov 2026 (r1 calendar computation)
flags.correction: British Columbia has been on UTC-7 all year since 8 Mar 2026 (Pacific Time, code PCT); no clocks turn back on 1 Nov 2026, so the 11 Nov wall clock is UTC-7. tzdata 2026b or later gives -7; older tzdata gives -8 and shifts the sun by 15 degrees.
flags.detail: Evidence (both opened r2): BC Gov release 2026AG0013 (clocks moved ahead 8 Mar 2026, 'the final time change', no change on 1 Nov) and companion release 2026CITZ0009 (PCT, no falling back); tz NEWS 2026b (22 Apr 2026) models permanent -07 from 1 Nov 2026 02:00 with abbreviation MST. P02-M01 pins tzdata at 2026b or later at build time and, from r3, stores explicit UTC instants.

flags.detail: Literal PST (UTC-8) = 11:00-13:00 on the wall clock (sun 18.4-23.2 degrees, shadow bearing 331-1, 300 m tower reaches 700-905 m). A wall-clock reading of 10:00-12:00 = 09:00-11:00 PST (sun 12.7-22.0 degrees, bearing 317-346, reach 740-1,340 m). The guideline was approved before the change and the reviewer reported an amendment dated 29 July 2026 whose treatment of the zone is unknown. Both windows run by default; PASS needs both. r3: ask the City (cddg@vancouver.ca or Planning), not the competition organisers, who do not interpret City rules; record the answer, its date and the sender; the second reader reads s.4.3.1.

The build fails if 'verified' lacks that record.

flags.claim: NorthFrame (angle CCW from model +Y) is meaningful on any imported model
flags.correction: Normalise every import to right-handed Z-up metres first (Y-up needs a +90 degree rotation about X, never a Y/Z swap) and run a blocking named-direction check (Stanley Park NW, BC Place SE, Burrard Inlet N-NE) with the site-plan labels placed in the model frame.
flags.detail: glTF 2.0 and three.js are Y-up right-handed (S54, S29); OBJ defines no up axis (S54); IFC TrueNorth is a direction in the project XY plane (S40). A Y/Z swap has determinant -1 and mirrors the plan, which passes every angle-agreement check but sends a NW shadow to the NE or SW. r3: without an underlay or edge picks the check compares the model with itself; the unit test now covers all four axis reflections.

flags.claim: PVGIS reference values queried with default settings (r1) are like-for-like with a Radiance/EPW run and with building-integrated facades
flags.correction: Compare with the same horizon setting (usehorizon=0 for a model without far terrain, or mask both with the PVGIS profile), convert aspect = azimuth - 180, and use mountingplace=building for BIPV faces.
flags.detail: r2 queries (S30): DEM horizon lowers annual irradiation on E by 9% (688 vs 753), NE by 10% (388 vs 429), SE by 5%, S by 2%; building-integrated yields are 1.6% (NE) to 2.8% (SW) below free-standing at the same irradiation (SW 800.1 vs 823.5 kWh/kWp). A +/-10% QA band would be breached by the horizon alone.

flags.claim: Georeferenced placement of the hypothetical VTC block
flags.detail: The VTC page gives no address or block; the brief labels directions on a rotated site plan. Which Table-1 spaces lie inside shadow reach depends on the chosen block (0.6-1.4 km reach), so M02 requires a SitePlacement input with a recorded rationale and a sensitivity mode over 3-5 candidate blocks. r3: candidate blocks are narrowed by the brief's cues (station on the neighbouring site, transit plaza diagonally across, arterial on a long side, retail high street, 79.2 x 144.8 m full block); a build-time OSM query for blocks of about 11,470 m2 beside subway or station entrances can shortlist them, and the VTC package, once obtained, overrides the choice. Results show the perturbation band and the noise-floor residual, never a rounded pass. r3: the earlier 1 m2 absolute floor is replaced by one raster cell area capped at 0.5% of the space area, and 0 for 'no shadow' rules.

flags.detail: No sourced cut-off exists; 10 degrees gives a 1.7 km context for 300 m and keeps about 5.0 of 8.2 daylight hours on 21 Dec (derived). The 120 W/m2 threshold is the WMO-linked sunshine definition via Wikipedia (S57); the WMO guide was not opened.

flags.claim: Pinning tzdata 2026b or later at build time guarantees UTC-7 on 11 Nov 2026 for every rule instant
flags.correction: Store explicit UTC instants per rule, computed server-side, and never convert local time in the browser; add a runtime assertion that the reading-B instant for 11 Nov 2026 10:00 equals 17:00Z (reading A 18:00Z, 22 Sept 10:00 = 17:00Z) and block M02 on failure.
flags.detail: Why false: build-time tzdata does not govern the entrant's browser, whose ICU/CLDR data may predate 2026b. tz NEWS 2026b (re-read r3) says the 1 Nov 2026 date is a workaround for a CLDR 48.1 limitation and that older slim zic files may ignore the transition; it does not name browsers (so the browser risk is derived). In such an environment reading B collapses into reading A and the 09:00-11:00 PST window, the longest reach, is never tested: a false PASS. SunCalc itself is safe when given a Date built from a UTC epoch (S28).

flags.claim: A SolarEnvelope or robust PASS from the 4 Basic-study instants gives the maximum compliant massing for a continuous 10:00-16:00 window
flags.correction: Build the envelope and every compliance result from a swept window (hull of shadows between consecutive instants at most 15 min apart, or continuous azimuth-indexed sun table); keep the 4-instant output only as the Basic study submission sheet, labelled 'format, not compliance'; transcribe per rule whether the City judges instants or the window.
flags.detail: Reproduced in r3 with the NOAA equations (S62): 22 Sept azimuth moves 33.0, 39.0 and 33.7 degrees across the 2-hour steps (125.9, 158.9, 197.9, 231.6); the tip of a 300 m shadow moves 30-59 m per 15 min on 22 Sept, and 57-174 m for 305 m on 11 Nov (UTC-7), so even 25 instants can miss a small space unless hulled. Equinox tips run on straight lines (chord deviation 0.002 m); the 11 Nov deviation is 0.4 m per 15 min (derived).

flags.claim: A site-centred disc of radius H / tan(lowest altitude) is a complete baseline context for every M02 output
flags.correction: Use the site reach disc plus each in-reach space's sun wedge, with radius (H_max + level difference) / tan(lowest altitude in its window), and print 'baseline incomplete: new shadow overstated (conservative)' where the baseline relies on 2009 footprints or missing approved towers.
flags.detail: r3 critic: existing towers that already shade a space can stand up to the shadow reach beyond it, outside a site-centred disc. Partly reproduced: along one sun ray every blocker for new shadow lies within the site-centred disc (derived), but existing, cumulative, total-shadow and coverage figures depend on all towers within reach of the receiver, so the wedges are required. Direction of the bias: a missing baseline tower lowers baseline shadow, so new shadow is overstated and the envelope over-restrictive.

flags.claim: A draft source corroborates the approved text: Robson 10:00-15:00, the Sun Yat-Sen absolute rule and the 4-instant Basic study are 'verified_secondary'
flags.correction: Use the evidence value 'draft_only' for Robson 10-15 and the Sun Yat-Sen absolute rule, and 'unverified' for the 4-instant Basic study; reserve 'verified_secondary' for content that an opened source states about the approved text.
flags.detail: Why false: the 2025 draft coverage (S06) is superseded text; UDI (S07, final) says only that Robson is 'similar' and Daily Hive (S04) names the garden without timing. No opened source states the 4 instants of the Basic study. Badge colour now comes from evidence, the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour from history.

flags.detail: Editable team presets with no sourced value; the City tolerance for new shadow is unknown. Chord deviations (0.002 m on 22 Sept, 0.4 m on 11 Nov per 15 min) are derived and should be re-computed by the tool as regression fixtures.

notes: Method and caveats (r3, 21 Oct 2026). The WebSearch budget was exhausted before work began, so research used direct fetches, the browser pane for HTML pages (City of Vancouver solar-access and CDDG pages, the City Clerk's agenda pages for 23 July 2025, 17 Sept 2025 and 4 Feb 2026, the competition page) and an independent pure-Python implementation of the NOAA solar equations to reproduce every solar fixture and the sweep numbers. Every PDF on guidelines.vancouver.ca, vancouver.ca/files and council.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 and none was downloaded (a download needs the user's own action), so the Downtown Peninsula guideline, the committee reports and the updated memo are still unread: S02 and S16 stay opened=false and M02 ships in EXPLORATION mode with no PASS/FAIL badge until the gate in the metric 'Evidence gate and release mode' is met. The email modal on the competition page was not submitted. Main r3 changes: swept-window compliance and envelope instead of 4 instants; explicit UTC rule instants with a runtime self-test; VTC package first; receiver-wedge baseline context; per-rule evidence including draft_only; label-aligned mirror check; EPW hour-ending alignment; tower-position sweep, 9.0 FSR capacity check, board shadow sheet and sibling-tower exposure folded into M02 and M08 (8-module cap). Badge rule: colour from evidence (verified green, verified_secondary blue, draft_only orange, unverified grey hatched, team_assumption amber), FALSE ASSUMPTION colour from history; status is a legacy field and a schema test fails if it implies more confidence than evidence. Team actions before any board claim: (1) by 29 Oct, request the VTC package with a team member's email and start the Table-1 transcription; download the guideline PDF in an ordinary browser, log page numbers, cover date and SHA-256, second reader confirms; read the 17 Sept 2025 memo; (2) ask the City (cddg@vancouver.ca) for the cenotaph clock and total-or-new basis; (3) re-check the posted CDDG solar text at the 13 Nov gate; (4) decide the platform licence given the AGPL components. Core by 13 Nov: M01, M02 Stage A, M03 (no small multiples), M06 (28-34 dev-days plus 3-5 data days against about 34 person-days available: see the capacity flag and cut list); v1 by 10 Dec: M02 Stage B, M04, M07, M08; roadmap: M05. Evidence labels: the output status enum lacks verified_secondary and draft_only, so metrics carry extra 'history' and 'evidence' fields; 'verified' is reserved for team-opened primary sources. Derived numbers must be recomputed by the tool and kept as regression fixtures. Decision Trees A-C exist as companion PDFs although the reviewer said otherwise; clause numbers remain the key.
